reader.requirement: At 1985 the KEY phrase's data-name-1 of START on an indexed file must be either (a) a prime or alternate record key of file-name-1, or (b) an alphanumeric item within a record of the file whose leftmost position coincides with a record key's leftmost position and whose length does not exceed that key's; anything else (longer, offset, numeric, alphabetic, alphanumeric-edited, outside the file's records, reference-modified, a table element) is refused, and a legal generic operand positions by comparison on the shorter length (GR4). The witnesses cover the refusal half (class mismatch, outside the record, too long, alphanumeric-edited) only.

edition-consulted.switches: ctx.Edition.SubscriptedClauseOperands (EditionInfo: Year == 2002): when false an operand subject to OCCURS is refused (COBOL0862); 85 takes false, as 2023 does

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule's range: 1985 SR4b's 'category alphanumeric' and 2023 SR6b2's 'same class, category and usage as that record key' coincide at 85 because the 1985 record key must itself be alphanumeric (§1985:IX.2.7.3 SR2, enforced: COBOL0863 at --std 85)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the refusal half (numeric class mismatch, outside the record, too long, alphanumeric-edited); the accepting half (prime, alternate, generic prefix in another record, a group prefix) and the runtime positioning are not exercised

reader.notes: BindStart asks KeyIndexOfKeyItem (SR4a) then GenericKeyIndex (SR4b: in a record of the file, leftmost-coincident, same class/category/usage as the key, not longer). A group item at the key's leftmost position (IX3-GRP) is accepted as alphanumeric; 1985 defines category only for elementary items and treats a group's class as alphanumeric (§1985:IV.4.3.3), so this reading is the natural one, stated here as the one interpretive point. Diagnostics cite the 2023 clause numbers (wording only).

refuter.evidence: r4-grpkey.cob at --std 85 (runs/r4-grpkey-002, EXIT 0), with a USE declarative so §1985:IX.4.9.3 SR3 / IX.4.5.3 SR7 hold. RECORD KEY IS KGRP is a group (X(2) plus 9(2)), which 1985 classes alphanumeric. START KEY > KP (an X(2) REDEFINES prefix in the same record) printed 'REDEF> THREE 00' (CC03 is the first key whose 2-character prefix exceeds BB). START KEY = IX2-PFX (X(3) in another record) printed 'PFX3= TWO 00'. START KEY > KGRP (the group key) printed 'GRP> TWO 00'. So SR4b's 'any data item of category alphanumeric' is admitted against a group key, in the same record and in another one, and GR4's shorter-length comparison holds. SameClassCategoryUsage does not refuse an elementary prefix of a group key. The reader's refusal probes (longer, offset, numeric, edited, alphabetic, outside the record, OCCURS, ref-mod) stand. cite.py: 'OK §1985:IX.4.7.3 SR4b the text is in SR4b' ('whose length is not greater than the length of that record key').
